answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, slashable bond in a vault before it can earn reputation-weighted rewards. The protocol randomly samples agents to complete costly, verifiable tasks; a fraud proof lets anyone show that several identities reuse the same operator or submit coordinated answers, triggering bond loss and removal of their rewards. A genuine newcomer can build standing over time, like recovering a relic after a comet’s pass, but an attacker must fund every identity and risk losing those deposits, making large-scale Sybils expensive rather than merely easy to create.
